items.title: Welcome to Kyoushitsu B!
items.text: Kyoushitsu B is a Wiki Database for Mobile Rhythm Games.

items.title: きょうしつ (kyo-u-shi-tsu)
items.text: classroom - a place where one learns or gains knowledge and experience

items.title: What is the purpose of Kyoushitsu B?
items.text: The purpose of this database is to provide you with the best information to get better at your favorite rhythm games, along with resources to make your rhythm game experience the best it can possibly be! You will find information about specific pattern names, strategies to improve on these specific patterns, among other rhythm game related ideas. There will also be guides to optimize your device to make sure it is running at its best for rhythm games!

items.title: billiam
items.text:
My name is billiam, a content creator who currently makes Project SEKAI and tech-related content!

In my free time, I like to play rhythm games like Project SEKAI. I also enjoy watching anime, reading manga, and playing visual novels.

My favorite characters in Project SEKAI are Saki Tenma and Honami Mochizuki.

My favorite anime is Clannad and its sequel, Clannad: After Story. It's an old slice of life anime from 2008 and is also the first anime series I have ever watched. I don't think a piece of media has moved me as much as this series has, so it's something that I won't be able to forget for a very, very long time if not ever.

From time to time, I also watch tech videos and dabble in computer/mobile device related projects such as PC building, keyboard building, custom software installation, software configuration, and more.

As the creator of Kyoushitsu B, I hope the information found in this Wiki will be valuable towards your next Full Combo or All Perfect!

- billiam

items.title: What Should I Look For in a Device?
items.text:
To ensure the best possible experience with rhythm games, it is vital that you choose the right device for this purpose. There are thousands upon thousands of different devices to choose from, each with their own set of unique specifications, but it is possible to narrow the choice down to a small number of devices.

Note

It is highly recommended to play on the devices you already own, and to upgrade only when necessary. If you are currently looking to purchase a new device, you may also want to consider how you will be using the device outside of rhythm games to maximize its effective value.

items.title: Display
items.text: • 10-12" Diagonally | 120hz Refresh Rate | 240hz Touch Sampling Rate

items.text:
• Android: Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 or Higher
  • iOS/iPadOS: Apple A14 or Higher, Apple M1 or Higher

items.title: Should You Play on a Tablet or a Phone?
items.text: Generally speaking, a tablet will be the best choice for the following reasons:

items.title: Increased Screen Size
items.text: Most phones have screen sizes anywhere from about 4" to 7". Most tablets, on the other hand, have double the screen sizes, with many well known tablets having anywhere from 8" (Lenovo Legion Y700 Series) to as much as 14" (Samsung Galaxy Tab Ultra Series). The increase in screen size will not only improve the visibility of notes, but will also increase the perceived hitbox size, making thinner notes significantly easier to tap.

items.title: Improved Multi-Finger Gameplay
items.text:
The increase in screen sizes will improve multi-finger placement. With a phone, attempting any four-key to six-key patterns will have your fingers in a cramped position, which may restrict hand movement.

Some manufacturers limit the amount of fingers that can be registered on the screen at once. For instance, Apple's iPhone will only register up to five fingers at any given moment, which is a behavior that is consistent with every iPhone in Apple's lineup.

items.title: Minimizing Interruptions
items.text: Playing rhythm games on a phone increases the chances of your device being interrupted by phone calls and messages. Depending on how many apps and background services are on your device, it is also more likely for the gameplay to experience stuttering. Putting rhythm games on a separate tablet minimizes the chances for interruptions to affect your gameplay, often resulting in a smoother experience.
